declare: `on: event: { table, op }` starts the flow after a row of `table` is written through the API. `table` is the SQL table name as in `/api/<table>` (the schema's `@@map` name, not the model name), matched exactly. A name that is no table of the app (the model name, another letter case, a framework table such as `_benmore_users`, a typo) is refused when the file is written, with the table to write named; a table only a migration creates is accepted. An app that already has such a flow keeps loading and logs it when the flows are registered: the flow never runs. `op` is insert, update or delete; any other value, or none, is refused when the file is written. on.event reads only these two keys (`when:` and `transaction:` are refused): filter with an `if:` step.
starts_on: Auto-CRUD create, update, delete and restore (an update), batch writes (one run per row), /api/_transaction, workflow transitions and POST /api/_groups/create: the writes listed in api({at:'hooks'}) → triggers. A flow's or cron job's own SQL, NDJSON /ingest and bulk import start no event flow.
values: The row's columns are `${{ name }}` and `:name`; `${{ params.<name> }}` reads them too. insert: the stored row, defaults and created_at included. update: the row after the change, plus `old_<column>` for every column before it. delete: the row as it was. In all three `user_id`, `user_email` and `user_role` are the signed-in caller who made the write, in place of same-named columns: when an admin edits another user's row `user_id` is the admin and `old_user_id` the stored owner, and a delete has no `old_` values, so the owner of a row someone else deleted is not in the event. There is no `${{ user.* }}` object.
runs: After the write has committed, in the background: the write's answer never changes because of the flow and normally does not wait for it (it waits when 32 event runs are already in flight). Each SQL statement commits on its own. A failing step ends the run after its on_error handler; statements that already ran stay, nothing is retried, and the only trace is the log line `FLOW ERROR [<flow>] <error>`. respond and redirect do nothing here. Several flows on one table and op all run, in no fixed order. Before-hooks and a SQL-only on_update hook have already run inside the write; the other hooks are queued jobs of their own.
yaml_example:
# flows/task-done-log.yaml - when a task becomes done, log it and tell its owner
on:
  event:
    table: tasks          # the SQL table name (as in /api/tasks), not the model name
    op: update            # insert | update | delete
jobs:
  log:
    steps:
      - if: ${{ status }} == 'done' && ${{ old_status }} != 'done'
        steps:
          - run: sql      # user_id is who made the change, old_user_id the stored owner
            with:
              query: "INSERT INTO task_events (task_id, kind, actor_id, user_id) VALUES (:id, 'done', :user_id, :old_user_id)"
          - if: ${{ user_id }} != ${{ old_user_id }}
            run: notify
            with:
              user_id: ${{ old_user_id }}
              title: "Task done: ${{ title }}"
              link: "/tasks/${{ id }}"
